description: Curated catalog of skills, connectors, agents and libraries for designing and building dashboards. Source of truth for docs/tools/ and the showcase site. Edit here, then run `node scripts/build.mjs`.

tiers.meaning: Use in most projects; skip only with a reason.
Useful add-on when the situation fits.
Only for a specific need (named in use_when).

kinds.meaning: A Claude skill, invoked by name (e.g. via the Skill tool or /name).
An MCP connector or CLI to an external service.
An open-source library or hosted service used in the code.
An open-source repository or method to study and apply (not installed as a dependency).

categories.name: Process & Planning
categories.blurb: Skills that keep the agent disciplined: brainstorm, spec, plan, then execute in small verified steps.

categories.name: Discovery & Research
categories.blurb: Turn interviews, voice notes, meeting transcripts and playbooks into clear needs and journeys.

categories.name: Brand & Visual Direction
categories.blurb: Decide what the product should feel like: positioning, palette, type, logo and mood boards.

categories.name: UI / UX Design
categories.blurb: Screen design, interaction design, design systems and critique, from flows to finished screens.

categories.name: UX Polish Rules
categories.blurb: Small, strict rule-sets (spacing, type, motion, loaders, empty states) that separate premium from generic.

categories.name: Dashboards & Data Viz
categories.blurb: KPI tiles, charts, report layouts and honest data presentation.

categories.name: CRM & Sales Workflows
categories.blurb: Pipeline logic, follow-ups, call summaries, lead triage. The functionality behind a CRM dashboard.

categories.name: Frontend Engineering
categories.blurb: Build production-quality UI incrementally, grounded in official docs.

categories.name: Testing, Review & Accessibility
categories.blurb: Prove it works: browser tests, audits, code review, security and verification gates.

categories.name: Deploy & Operate
categories.blurb: GitHub and Vercel: repos, previews, production deploys, logs and rollbacks.

categories.name: Connectors & Data Sources
categories.blurb: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, spreadsheets and meeting recorders that feed the CRM.

categories.blurb: Calendar views, provider APIs, agent connectors, ICS feeds and booking. Full repo directory: catalog/calendars.json.

categories.name: Media & Assets
categories.blurb: Images, icons, illustrations, sound and video for a polished product.

categories.name: Code Libraries & Services
categories.blurb: The recommended open-source building blocks and hosted services for the stack.

categories.name: Docs, Handover & Training
categories.blurb: Make the client self-sufficient: docs, decision records and guided onboarding.

phases.name: Discover
phases.goal: Understand the business, the people and the job the dashboard must do.
phases.gate: A written summary of needs that the client has confirmed.

phases.name: Define
phases.goal: Turn needs into a scoped spec: data model, screens, v1 features, non-goals.
phases.gate: spec.md approved; v1 scope fits in one page.

phases.name: Direction
phases.goal: Choose the look and feel: theme, typography, palette, tone of voice.
phases.gate: One visual direction chosen from 2-3 options; tokens written.

phases.name: Design
phases.goal: Information architecture, page patterns, component inventory, key states.
phases.gate: Every screen has a named page pattern and its empty/loading/error states are defined.

phases.name: Build
phases.goal: Implement in small, deployable slices on the recommended stack.
phases.gate: Each slice deployed to a Vercel preview and checked in a real browser.

phases.name: Polish & QA
phases.goal: Apply the rulebook, audit UX and accessibility, test on phone and desktop.
phases.gate: QA checklist passes; no open severity-1 findings.

phases.name: Ship
phases.gate: Production URL live; rollback path known.

phases.name: Handover
phases.goal: Transfer ownership and teach the client to change it with their own AI.
phases.gate: Client made one change themselves via Claude -> GitHub -> Vercel.

tools.name: Brainstorming
tools.summary: Structured, question-by-question exploration of intent and requirements before any creative or build work starts.
use_when: Starting a new dashboard or a new major feature
The request is fuzzy ("make it nice", "something like a CRM")
avoid_when: Small, fully specified fixes
The spec is already approved; go to writing-plans
how_to_use: Ask one question at a time; propose 2-3 approaches with a recommendation
Write the agreed design to docs/ before building

tools.name: Idea Refine
tools.summary: Divergent-then-convergent ideation: generates options, then narrows to the strongest with explicit criteria.
use_when: Choosing between dashboard concepts or feature ideas
The client has many wishes and v1 needs a focus
avoid_when: The direction is already decided
how_to_use: Feed it the client's goals and constraints; ask for 3 concepts scored against them

tools.name: Spec-Driven Development
tools.summary: Writes a structured specification (goals, users, scope, acceptance criteria, non-goals) before code exists.
use_when: After discovery, before any design or code
Requirements live only in voice notes or chat
avoid_when: Tiny changes to an existing, documented feature
how_to_use: Use templates/spec.md as the output shape
Every v1 feature needs a testable acceptance criterion

tools.name: Planning & Task Breakdown
tools.summary: Breaks a spec into small, ordered, verifiable tasks with dependencies.
use_when: The spec is approved and you need a build order
A task feels too big to start
avoid_when: There is no spec yet: write one first
how_to_use: Slice vertically: each task ends in something visible on a preview URL

tools.name: Writing Plans
tools.summary: Produces a step-by-step implementation plan file an agent (or a later session) can execute faithfully.
use_when: Multi-session work where context will be lost between sessions
Handing work to subagents
avoid_when: One-file changes
how_to_use: Save plans in docs/plans/ so the client's AI can resume later

tools.name: Executing Plans
tools.summary: Executes a written plan task by task with checkpoints, as the implementer in the current session.
use_when: A plan file exists and you are implementing it yourself
avoid_when: No written plan exists
how_to_use: Tick tasks off in the plan file as you go

tools.name: Subagent-Driven Development
tools.summary: Runs independent plan tasks through fresh subagents with review between tasks.
use_when: Large builds with many independent tasks
avoid_when: Small projects: overhead outweighs benefit
Tasks that share files heavily
how_to_use: Use only after the plan is stable

tools.name: Dispatching Parallel Agents
tools.summary: Fans out 2+ independent tasks (e.g. separate audits) to parallel agents.
use_when: Running UX, accessibility and performance audits at once
avoid_when: Tasks that depend on each other's output
how_to_use: Give every agent a self-contained brief and expected output format

tools.name: Using Agent Skills
tools.summary: Meta-skill: how to discover and invoke the right skill for a task.
use_when: Starting a session in a new environment with many installed skills
avoid_when: You already know which skill applies: just use it
how_to_use: This repo's catalog/tools.json is the curated version of this for dashboards

tools.name: Karpathy Guidelines
tools.summary: Behavioral guardrails against common LLM coding mistakes: over-engineering, unrequested changes, hidden assumptions.
use_when: Any coding session, especially when a non-developer client is directing changes
how_to_use: Make surgical changes; state assumptions; define how success is verified

tools.name: Context Engineering
tools.summary: Sets up rules files and context so future agent sessions start with the right knowledge.
use_when: Writing the client project's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
Agent output quality is degrading over a long project
how_to_use: Keep always-loaded files short; link to deeper docs

tools.name: Research Synthesis
tools.summary: Distills transcripts, interviews and notes into themes, insights and recommendations.
use_when: You have the client's voice memo, a meeting transcript (Fathom, Otter, etc.) or interview notes
Several sources need to be merged into one picture
avoid_when: There is no raw research yet: plan it with user-research first
how_to_use: Quote the client verbatim for each insight
End with 'needs', 'pains', 'must-haves', 'nice-to-haves'

tools.name: User Research
tools.summary: Plans research: interview guides, research questions, usability tests and surveys.
use_when: Preparing for an in-person conversation with the client
Planning a usability test of a prototype
avoid_when: You already have enough input to synthesize
how_to_use: Start from templates/discovery-questions.md

tools.name: UX Research (deep)
tools.summary: Deeper research methodology: scripts, test plans, recruiting, qualitative analysis.
use_when: Testing the finished dashboard with the client's team
avoid_when: A single-user tool where talking to the owner is enough
how_to_use: Use for a 30-minute think-aloud test before handover

tools.name: Journey Mapping
tools.summary: Customer journey maps, service blueprints and empathy maps.
use_when: Mapping the client's client lifecycle (lead -> client -> repeat) to derive pipeline stages
Finding where follow-ups fall through the cracks
avoid_when: Purely visual tasks
how_to_use: The stages of the journey usually become the pipeline columns

tools.name: UX Strategy
tools.summary: Jobs-to-be-done, opportunity mapping and UX metrics tied to business outcomes.
use_when: Deciding what the dashboard should measure and why
avoid_when: Small internal tools with obvious goals
how_to_use: Use JTBD to phrase each screen's one job

tools.name: Call Summary
tools.summary: Turns a call transcript or notes into a follow-up email, an internal summary and proposed CRM updates.
use_when: Processing the recorded client meeting
Later: a CRM feature that turns meeting notes into record updates
avoid_when: No transcript or notes exist
how_to_use: Run on the Fathom transcript first to extract action items and requirements

tools.name: Deep Research
tools.summary: Multi-source web research with comparison and synthesis.
use_when: Researching the client's industry, competitors or CRM conventions in their niche
avoid_when: Facts already in the client's documents
how_to_use: Ask for a sourced comparison table, not prose

tools.name: File Reading (PDF / DOCX / XLSX)
tools.summary: Read and extract content from the client's playbook, spreadsheets and documents.
use_when: The client sends a PDF playbook or an existing spreadsheet of contacts
how_to_use: Extract the playbook's stages, rules and terminology into docs/ before designing

tools.name: Choose What to Build
tools.summary: Prioritization grounded in how others in your network handled similar decisions.
use_when: The wish-list is long and needs ruthless v1 prioritization
avoid_when: Scope is already small and clear

tools.name: Choose Metrics
tools.summary: Helps decide which metrics to track (the KPI strip).
use_when: Picking the max-5 KPI tiles for the overview page
how_to_use: Each KPI must drive a decision; otherwise drop it

tools.name: Brand Strategy
tools.summary: Positioning, audience, personality and promise. The 'why' behind the look.
use_when: The client's business has no clear brand yet
avoid_when: The client already has a brand guide: reuse it
how_to_use: Keep to one page; the dashboard is internal, so personality matters more than positioning

tools.name: Brand Brief
tools.summary: Turns brand decisions into a practical production brief: principles, assets, constraints.
use_when: Translating 'I want it calm and luxurious' into concrete design inputs
avoid_when: No brand decisions exist yet: run brand-strategy or ask the client
how_to_use: Output feeds templates/design-direction.md

tools.name: Brand Identity System
tools.summary: Logo concepts, color, typography and identity guidelines.
use_when: The client wants a small logo mark or wordmark for the dashboard
avoid_when: Just choosing a dashboard theme: use the themes in design-system/

tools.name: Brand Review
tools.summary: Checks assets and screens against the brand for consistency and drift.
use_when: Before handover, to check every screen follows the chosen direction

tools.name: Brand Style (Small Business)
tools.summary: Captures a small business's look from a website link or a plain-words description.
use_when: The client has a website or Instagram: extract colors and tone from it quickly
avoid_when: Formal identity work
how_to_use: Paste the client's website URL; map the result to design-system tokens

tools.name: Creative Direction
tools.summary: Explores visual direction: mood boards, palettes, typography systems, art direction.
use_when: Producing 2-3 distinct visual directions for the client to choose from
avoid_when: Direction already chosen: move to design
how_to_use: Present directions as live themes (see site/ Themes page), not abstract adjectives

tools.name: Map Design (extract DESIGN.md)
tools.summary: Extracts a design language from a screenshot, URL, Figma file or codebase into a DESIGN.md.
use_when: The client shows apps or sites whose look they love
Documenting the final token set
how_to_use: Run on 2-3 reference screenshots, then merge into one token set

tools.name: Theme Factory
tools.summary: Ten preset color/font themes that can be applied to any artifact, or a custom one.
use_when: Quick theme exploration for a prototype
avoid_when: Production theming: use design-system/tokens.css

tools.name: CoDesign: Create
tools.summary: Generates visual designs (posters, social posts, decks, mood boards) on the IMG.LY CoDesign canvas.
use_when: Making a mood board or brand board to show the client
Making a launch graphic for the client
avoid_when: Building the dashboard UI itself: that is code
how_to_use: Load codesign:handbook first; run codesign:judge before calling it done

tools.name: CoDesign: Brand
tools.summary: Applies a brand kit to an existing CoDesign design by rule.
use_when: Re-skinning a mood board or graphic to the chosen brand

tools.name: Adobe Fonts
tools.summary: Finds and previews licensable typefaces with metadata.
use_when: Searching for a distinctive typeface beyond Google Fonts
avoid_when: Google Fonts already covers the need (easier to self-host on Vercel)

tools.name: Adobe Firefly Boards
tools.summary: Builds shareable mood/inspiration boards.
use_when: Collecting visual references with the client

tools.name: Frontend Design
tools.summary: Distinctive, intentional visual design: subject-grounded palette and typography, no templated defaults.
use_when: Any time you create or reshape UI
The output risks looking like a generic AI SaaS template
avoid_when: Pure backend work
how_to_use: Ground choices in the client's world (their industry, materials, vocabulary)
Avoid: single accented headline word, ALL-CAPS labels, decorative 01/02/03 numbering, entrance animation on every section

tools.name: Design Elevation
tools.summary: Turns functional output into polished design: functional and perceptual patterns, interrogating every default.
use_when: The dashboard works but looks 'fine' rather than premium
avoid_when: Before a working version exists (function first)
how_to_use: Dashboard structure: KPI bar -> primary chart -> supporting charts -> detail tables
Question every default: font, radius, shadow, color

tools.name: Design (features & flows)
tools.summary: Designs features, flows and screens using an existing design system.
use_when: Composing the contact detail page, pipeline board or add-lead flow from components
avoid_when: No design system exists yet: run ds-make first

tools.name: Design System: Make
tools.summary: Creates and versions tokens, components and patterns.
use_when: Turning the chosen direction into tokens and a component list
avoid_when: One-off prototypes
how_to_use: Start from design-system/tokens.css instead of from scratch

tools.name: Design Systems (deep)
tools.summary: Tokens, component specs, naming conventions and governance.
use_when: Documenting the system so the client's AI keeps it consistent
avoid_when: Small single-page tools

tools.name: Design System Audit
tools.summary: Audits components for hard-coded values and naming inconsistencies; documents variants.
use_when: Before handover, find hard-coded colors and spacing that bypass tokens

tools.name: Interaction Design
tools.summary: Microinteractions, state machines, gestures, error prevention and product behavior across states.
use_when: Designing drag-and-drop pipeline moves, quick-add, inline edit, undo
avoid_when: Static content pages
how_to_use: Specify every component's states: default, hover, focus, active, loading, empty, error, disabled

tools.name: Design Critique (heuristics)
tools.summary: Heuristic evaluation against usability heuristics, UX laws and IA principles.
use_when: Reviewing screens before showing the client
how_to_use: Ask for severity-ranked findings with concrete fixes

tools.name: Design Critique (quick)
tools.summary: Faster structured feedback on hierarchy, usability and consistency from a screenshot.
use_when: Fast feedback on a single screenshot

tools.name: Design Review
tools.summary: Reviews designs against heuristics, accessibility, design-system compliance, visual quality and motion.
use_when: Pre-handover review of the whole product

tools.name: UX Writing
tools.summary: User-centered interface copy: buttons, labels, errors, notifications, onboarding, empty states.
use_when: Writing every label, button and message in the CRM
how_to_use: Verb-first buttons ('Add client', not 'Submit')
Use the client's own vocabulary from the playbook

tools.name: UX Copy (quick)
tools.summary: Quick microcopy and CTA wording.
use_when: Naming a single button or wording one error

tools.name: Design Handoff
tools.summary: Developer spec sheets: tokens, props, states, breakpoints, motion.
use_when: Design was done in Figma or by a separate designer and must be handed to the coding agent
avoid_when: Designer and builder are the same agent

tools.name: Superdesign
tools.summary: Designs or redesigns UI on the Superdesign canvas with multiple AI models, producing variations fast.
use_when: Producing several layout variations of the overview page to show the client
avoid_when: Final production code
how_to_use: Use for exploration; rebuild the chosen variation with tokens in code

tools.name: 21st.dev UI
tools.summary: Find, install and generate React UI components (dashboards, forms, navbars) from 21st.dev.
use_when: Need a polished starting point for a complex component (command palette, data table, calendar)
avoid_when: Components that already exist in shadcn/ui
how_to_use: Re-skin installed components with project tokens; delete decorative extras (anti-slop)

tools.name: Web Artifacts Builder
tools.summary: Builds multi-component React + Tailwind + shadcn HTML artifacts on claude.ai.
use_when: A clickable prototype to show the client on claude.ai before the real build
avoid_when: The production app (use the Next.js repo)

tools.name: Figma (read/write)
tools.summary: Prerequisite for all Figma MCP writes; create and edit Figma files.
use_when: The client or a designer works in Figma
avoid_when: No Figma account: design in code instead
how_to_use: Always load before any use_figma call

tools.name: Figma: Design to Code
tools.summary: Implements a Figma design as code.
use_when: A Figma mockup exists and must be built

tools.name: Figma: Generate Design
tools.summary: Pushes an app page or layout from code into Figma.
use_when: The client wants editable Figma copies of the screens

tools.name: Figma: Generate Library
tools.summary: Builds a Figma design-system library from the codebase tokens and components.
use_when: Handing a designer a Figma library that matches the code

tools.name: Page Patterns
tools.summary: Forces one named page pattern (list, detail, form, dashboard, settings, board, calendar, split pane, analytics, inbox) before any page markup.
use_when: Before creating any new screen or route
avoid_when: Components inside a page (charts, tiles)
how_to_use: Overview = Dashboard (glance, max 5 KPIs, read-only)
Pipeline = Board
Clients = List
One client = Detail

tools.name: Surfaces (inline / slide-over / page)
tools.summary: Routes each task to the lightest surface: inline edit, slide-over or a dedicated page; named confirmations for destructive actions.
use_when: Adding any modal, drawer, dialog or inline edit
how_to_use: <10s task: slide-over; >=10s or multi-step: its own page; single field: inline, zero layout shift
Destructive confirm names the item: "Delete client 'Harbor & Pine'?"

tools.name: Anti-Slop
tools.summary: Removes AI-template clichés: rainbow gradients, glassmorphism, cartoon empty states, decorative pills and input icons.
use_when: Reviewing any AI-generated UI
Before every client demo
how_to_use: Delete decoration, never structure (keep table frames, dividers, search)

tools.name: Colour Palette & Elevation
tools.summary: 60-30-10 color distribution; depth via 1px subtle borders then soft shadows (alpha < 0.08).
use_when: Choosing surfaces, borders, shadows, accents or dark-mode depth
how_to_use: Accent only on actions, active nav, links and focus; never on big fills

tools.name: Typography
tools.summary: Max 3 weights (never > 700), 16/14/12px base sizes, line-height inversely related to size.
use_when: Setting type styles or fixing noisy hierarchy
how_to_use: Table cells use 14-16px, never 12px
Hierarchy from size and spacing, not weight

tools.name: Spacing & Alignment
tools.summary: 8pt grid for components, 4pt for micro spacing, 65-75ch line length, cap-height icon alignment.
use_when: Laying out any screen

tools.name: Motion
tools.summary: Duration tokens 100/150/200/300ms, ease-out in / ease-in out, animate transform & opacity only, no bouncy chrome.
use_when: Adding any transition or animation
how_to_use: One motion language per product
No infinite decorative loops

tools.name: Transitions
tools.summary: Enter/exit patterns for overlays and lists with zero layout jump.
use_when: Animating drawers, dialogs, popovers, route changes, staggered lists
how_to_use: Slide-overs: translateX + opacity 200ms in, 150ms out

tools.name: Reduced Motion
tools.summary: Honors prefers-reduced-motion with instant or opacity-only fallbacks.
use_when: Every time motion is added

tools.name: Loaders
tools.summary: Loader by duration: none < 100ms, inline 100ms-1s, structural skeleton > 1s.
use_when: Adding spinners, skeletons or async fetches
how_to_use: Never a full-page spinner; skeletons mirror the real layout

tools.name: Empty States
tools.summary: Every empty view states what belongs there, why it matters, and gives one primary action; filtered-empty offers 'Clear filters'.
use_when: Building any list, board, table or first-run screen
how_to_use: Keep the page skeleton visible in the empty state

tools.name: Errors
tools.summary: Error copy never blames the user and always offers recovery.
use_when: Writing errors, toasts or failure states
how_to_use: Say what happened, why (if known), and what to do next

tools.name: Forms
tools.summary: Validate on blur, clear errors instantly, fewer fields, always-clickable submit.
use_when: Building add-client, add-deal, settings or any form
how_to_use: Ask only for what v1 needs; everything else is optional later

tools.name: Labels
tools.summary: Visible labels on every input; placeholders only for format hints.
use_when: Any form field

tools.name: Smart Defaults
tools.summary: Intelligent defaults and draft persistence to avoid blank busywork.
use_when: Forms, dropdowns, preferences, multi-step entry
how_to_use: Default the follow-up date (e.g. +3 days) and the stage (first stage)

tools.name: Verbs (button labels)
tools.summary: Verb-first labels; bans OK, Submit, Proceed.
use_when: Any button, link or menu item

tools.name: Icon Buttons
tools.summary: Square icon buttons with required tooltips and keyboard shortcuts.
use_when: Toolbars, view toggles, export/filter controls
how_to_use: Hit area >= 44x44 even if the glyph is 16px

tools.name: Keyboard
tools.summary: Full keyboard access, visible focus rings, focus trap/restore for overlays.
use_when: Any interactive UI, especially the pipeline board and slide-overs
how_to_use: Drag-and-drop must have a keyboard alternative (Move to...)

tools.name: Viewports
tools.summary: Works from 375px to 1280px: no page overflow, collapsing chrome, 44px targets, no hover-only actions.
use_when: Every page, before calling it done
how_to_use: Test at 375 and 1280; tables/boards scroll inside their region only

tools.name: VectorLab UX Audit
tools.summary: Audits the current UI against every VectorLab rule at once.
use_when: Before finishing any UI work; before every client demo
how_to_use: Fix all hard-rule failures before showing the client

tools.name: VectorLab Setup (.ux-profile.md)
tools.summary: Writes a .ux-profile.md (aesthetic reference, bans, accessibility target, voice, icon library) that all polish skills read.
use_when: Once per project, right after the visual direction is chosen
how_to_use: Aesthetic reference for a calm premium CRM: 'Linear/Notion restraint, warm palette'

tools.name: Soundweaver (UI sounds)
tools.summary: Adds subtle contextual UI sound effects (click, success) to web projects.
use_when: The client explicitly wants a tactile, playful feel
avoid_when: Default: most business dashboards should be silent
how_to_use: Off by default with a settings toggle

tools.name: Dataviz (chart system)
tools.summary: Method for charts, stat tiles and dashboards that read as one system: form heuristic, color formula, mark specs, interaction rules.
use_when: Before writing ANY chart, KPI tile, sparkline or legend
how_to_use: Pick the chart from the question; one categorical palette; same look in light and dark

tools.name: Build Dashboard (HTML report)
tools.summary: Builds interactive self-contained HTML dashboards with KPI cards, charts, filters and tables.
use_when: A one-off reporting dashboard or a prototype of the analytics view
avoid_when: The CRM app itself (use the Next.js stack)
how_to_use: Borrow its KPI-card and filter layouts for the app's analytics page

tools.name: Data Visualization (Python)
tools.summary: Chart-type selection and design principles with matplotlib/seaborn/plotly.
use_when: Static charts for a report or proposal
avoid_when: Interactive in-app charts (use Recharts)

tools.name: Create Viz
tools.summary: Publication-quality charts from query results.
use_when: Exporting a chart image for a PDF report

tools.name: Explore Data
tools.summary: Profiles a dataset: shape, nulls, duplicates, distributions.
use_when: Importing the client's existing spreadsheet of contacts
how_to_use: Run before designing the import: find duplicates and missing emails

tools.name: Validate Data
tools.summary: QA an analysis: methodology, accuracy, bias.
use_when: Checking KPI calculations (pipeline value, win rate) are right

tools.name: Report Builder
tools.summary: Turns a plain-English description of a recurring report into defined metrics and a repeatable report.
use_when: The client wants a weekly/monthly emailed summary

tools.name: Business Pulse
tools.summary: One-page cross-functional business snapshot for owners.
use_when: Inspiration for what a small-business owner wants on one screen

tools.name: Analyze
tools.summary: Answers data questions from quick lookups to full analyses.
use_when: After launch: 'which lead source converts best?'

tools.name: CRM Autopilot
tools.summary: Keeps a CRM current from email, calendar and transcripts; drafts follow-ups on quiet deals.
use_when: Defining which updates the CRM should do automatically
Designing 'gone quiet' alerts
avoid_when: The client wants full manual control in v1
how_to_use: Use its behavior as the spec for v2 automations

tools.name: Sales Setup
tools.summary: First-run setup: checks connected tools and renders a starter sales dashboard.
use_when: Seeing what a sales starter dashboard contains, quickly

tools.name: Pipeline Review
tools.summary: Stage-by-stage pipeline health: coverage, aging, conversion and at-risk deals.
use_when: Designing the pipeline board and its health indicators
how_to_use: Aging (days in stage) and 'no next step' are the two most useful flags

tools.name: Deal Review
tools.summary: Single-opportunity deep dive: health, risks, qualification gaps, next actions.
use_when: Designing the deal/client detail page

tools.name: Deal Advance Gap
tools.summary: What is missing to advance a deal to the next stage, with owners and dates.
use_when: Designing stage-exit checklists from the client's playbook

tools.name: Deal Signals
tools.summary: Alert digest: quiet deals, slipping dates, renewals, competitor mentions.
use_when: Designing the 'Needs attention' panel on the overview

tools.name: Daily Briefing
tools.summary: Morning rundown: today's meetings, deals closing soon, waiting emails, top actions.
use_when: Designing the 'Today' home view
how_to_use: The Today view is usually the most-used screen of a small-business CRM

tools.name: Monday Brief
tools.summary: Weekly owner briefing combining business snapshot and saved reports.
use_when: Designing a 'This week' view or weekly email

tools.name: Log Activity
tools.summary: Logs a call, meeting or email to the right record from a description or transcript.
use_when: Designing the activity timeline and quick-log interaction

tools.name: Update Opportunity
tools.summary: Guided updates with before/after: stage, close date, next step, amount.
use_when: Designing the edit-deal slide-over

tools.name: CRM Hygiene Check
tools.summary: Audits records for missing fields, stale dates and stage mismatches.
use_when: Designing data-quality nudges; checking imported data

tools.name: Lead Triage
tools.summary: Scores and ranks inbound leads with talking points and follow-ups.
use_when: Designing a lead inbox and priority ranking

tools.name: Speed to Lead
tools.summary: Ensures no inbound lead goes unanswered; qualifies and drafts replies.
use_when: The client loses leads from web forms or DMs

Hold steps ~5 s, the result 6–8 s
